findings.issue_text: Missing test changes or validation evidence

The test 'tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found' sets up a mock for TopicRetriever.expects(:new) but the controller action actually calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic), so the mock setup does not match the implementation and the test would fail

spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb uses require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post' instead of the correct 'jobs/scheduled/poll_feed', indicating a copy-paste error that could also cause a LoadError if the file doesn't exist
embed_controller.rb:13-23 — When topic_id is found but the topic has been deleted, TopicView.new may raise an exception with no handling for deleted/missing topics
poll_feed.rb:30 — i.content is accessed without checking if it exists; SimpleRSS items may not always have a content field, causing NoMethodError for RSS feeds that only provide description
topic_embed.rb:41 — embed.post is accessed without checking if the associated post still exists; a deleted post would cause NoMethodError on the subsequent revisor call

topic_embed.rb:42 — PostRevisor#revise! is called with new_raw as the second argument but the updated signature expects new_raw to be a string of raw content; revisor revision may not respect cook_method: raw_html setting since post_revisor.rb doesn't set cook_method

topic_retriever.rb:45 — Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) is invoked synchronously from within perform_retrieve, which could block the RetrieveTopic worker on the entire feed poll and run outside the scheduler's intended context

poll_feed.rb:13 — sidekiq_options retry: false with hourly recurrence means transient HTTP/network errors during open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) will silently drop that hour's poll with no alerting or logging
poll_feed.rb:31 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) is vulnerable to SSRF; there's no validation that it's an http(s) URL or restriction against internal addresses
topic_embed.rb:55 — Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...) has no timeout, error handling, or response-size limit; a slow or huge remote page will hang the worker indefinitely
embed_controller.rb:28 — ensure_embeddable only checks a single embeddable_host with no support for multiple allowed hosts/subdomains

embed.js:11 — discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 for origin validation is substring-based and vulnerable to spoofing (e.g., http://eviltrout.com.evil.com would pass if discourseUrl is http://eviltrout.com); should use exact URL comparison
embed.html.erb:10 — parent.postMessage uses request.referer as targetOrigin; if referer is blank or invalid, postMessage silently fails to deliver with no fallback
best.html.erb:7 — @topic_view.topic.url is referenced even in the no posts branch; if topic_id_for_embed returns a topic with zero posts, .url may raise

embed_controller_spec.rb:50-52 — Test stubs TopicRetriever.new but the actual controller calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) asynchronously, not TopicRetriever directly; the test does not match the implementation
create_topic_embeds.rb:9 — embed_url is a string with no length limit; long URLs will truncate silently on MySQL or fail on insert depending on the adapter, with no explicit limit or model validation

post_revisor.rb:14 — Removing the return false if not should_revise? line changes behavior for all callers, causing unnecessary post revisions/edits across the entire app — a regression unrelated to the stated intent

topic_embed.rb:22 — The import appends I18n.t('embed.imported_from') with the raw URL inserted unescaped into an <a href='...'>; a malicious feed URL containing single quotes or HTML could break out of the attribute and inject markup
topic_embed.rb:60 — absolutize_urls only handles a and img relative URLs; other relative resources (srcset, CSS url(), source, video, iframe, etc.) are not absolutized, leading to broken resources

site_settings.yml:354 — embeddable_host has no validation that it's actually a hostname (not a full URL); if an admin enters http://eviltrout.com, the host comparison will always fail and embedding will be silently broken

poll_feed.rb:26 — User.where(username_lower: ...) returns nil silently if the configured embed_by_username user doesn't exist; the entire poll is silently skipped with no logging, making misconfiguration undetectable
Unrelated whitespace change in db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb causes scope drift
Unrelated force: true added to top_topics migration in db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb
lib/tasks/disqus.thor removes the --category option and its handling, causing an unrelated functional regression
lib/post_revisor.rb mixes an unrelated cosmetic blank-line removal with the functional skip_validations change
PR title mismatch: diff introduces a broad new embedding subsystem rather than just enhancing an existing validation system
Missing trailing newlines in several new/modified files (embed.css.scss, embed.html.erb, loading.html.erb, migrate_word_counts.rb)
Unbounded/unpaginated topic view retrieval: missing guard that the topic belongs to an embed context or is accessible to the embedding surface, leaking private/restricted topics
Referer origin check in embed_controller.rb is substring-based and breaks when `request.referer` is missing, causing all legitimate embeds to fail
`X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` set globally without origin hardening; combined with substring-based `postMessage` origin check in embed.js, allows origin-validation bypass
TOCTOU race in `TopicEmbed.import`: `where` then `create` is not atomic, allowing duplicate topics and orphaned rows from concurrent jobs
Missing foreign keys and no index on `topic_id` in `create_topic_embeds.rb` migration, leaving dangling records and linear lookups
`cook_method` has no DB-level CHECK constraint and uses a magic int default, allowing invalid values to be written directly
`content_sha1` duplicates post content hash and is bypassed by other revision paths, causing it to drift and become stale
Unbounded materialization / no dedup pagination over the feed in `poll_feed.rb`: iterates entire feed with no cap, last-seen record, or etag usage
N+1 queries / no filtering of already-imported items in `poll_feed.rb`: each item calls `TopicEmbed.import` doing its own lookup
`i.content` can be nil/missing in `poll_feed.rb`, causing `NoMethodError` and aborting the entire feed import without per-item rescue
`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `poll_feed.rb` is SSRF-vulnerable and unauthenticated, lacking scheme/host allowlists, redirect caps, or timeouts
`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously triggers full feed poll from within an on-demand job, coupling async paths and causing inefficiency
Throttle in `topic_retriever.rb` uses Redis `setnx`/`expire` non-atomically, risking a permanent lock if a crash occurs between the two calls
`import_remote` uses `open(url).read` with no scheme/host validation, creating an SSRF/XXE vector via the Disqus path
`raw_html` cook method bypasses the sanitization pipeline entirely, causing stored XSS in the embed surface when rendering unescaped RSS/HTML content
`postMessage` targetOrigin in `embed.html.erb` is `request.referer`, leaking embed height/structure to any parent and risking errors if referer is nil/invalid
`post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` in `best.html.erb` assume `user` is non-nil and loaded per post, causing N+1 queries and crashes for deleted users
`skip_validations: true` on imported posts bypasses rate limits, spam checks, and required metadata, creating a validation-free write surface
`@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` in `post_revisor.rb` changes default revision semantics, allowing any future caller to unintentionally bypass validations
User lookup by `username_lower` in `topic_retriever.rb` is not fail-fast validated; if the setting names a non-existent user, the embed never completes
`absolutize_urls` in `topic_embed.rb` only handles `href`/`src` starting with `/`, missing protocol-relative URLs, `../` paths, and srcset attributes
`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` in `embed.js` is a substring-origin bug, allowing spoofed origins that contain the discourse URL substring
`force: true` added to existing migration `create_top_topics.rb` is destructive and not idempotent-safe across rolling deploys
Trailing newline removed in `migrate_word_counts.rb` and whitespace-only diff mixes unrelated concerns into the PR
`import_remote` in the Disqus path has no `embeddable_host` check, allowing off-host links to be fetched and imported, muddling the ownership boundary
`belongs_to :topic` / `:post` in `topic_embed.rb` lacks `optional`/inverse and no uniqueness on `post_id`, allowing multiple embed rows per topic
db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb: Unrelated `force: true` in `create_table` is destructive and causes data loss if the table exists.
db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb: Contains unrelated whitespace changes and removes the newline at the end of the file.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor: Refactoring Disqus import to use `TopicEmbed.import_remote` causes functional regression by dropping support for the `category` option and ignoring original `created_at` timestamps.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js: `postMessage` origin validation uses `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, which is a flawed security pattern allowing substring matches to bypass instead of exact origin matching.
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb: `i.content.scrub` is called without checking if `i.content` is present, causing a `NoMethodError` if an RSS/Atom feed item lacks a content field.
app/models/topic_embed.rb: `absolutize_urls` hardcodes ports 80 and 443, failing for non-standard configurations and incorrectly appending ports; should use `uri.default_port`.
Stored XSS vulnerability: RSS feed content is stored and rendered as raw HTML without any sanitization, allowing attackers to inject script tags via the RSS feed.
Stored XSS vulnerability: URL is interpolated unescaped into an `<a href>` attribute in the imported_from footer, allowing attribute injection via malicious URLs.
Stored XSS vulnerability: `javascript:` URI schemes are not stripped from Readability-extracted links, allowing execution of attacker-controlled JavaScript when clicked.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test changes or validation evidence

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes substantial new test coverage for the added embedding/feed functionality: `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb`, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, and `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`. These directly exercise key validation/guard behavior (missing embed_url, missing host, referer checks, throttling, feed settings requirements, TopicEmbed import/update). Therefore the proposed finding that test changes/validation evidence are missing is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The test 'tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found' sets up a mock for TopicRetriever.expects(:new) but the controller action actually calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic), so the mock setup does not match the implementation and the test would fail

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no topic_id is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`; it does not instantiate `TopicRetriever` directly. However, the spec `"tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found"` sets expectations on `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`. Since that code path never calls `TopicRetriever`, the expectation will not be satisfied (and `Jobs.enqueue` will be invoked instead), so the test as written would fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb uses require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post' instead of the correct 'jobs/scheduled/poll_feed', indicating a copy-paste error that could also cause a LoadError if the file doesn't exist

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, the top-level require is `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'`, but the spec is for `Jobs::PollFeed` (implemented in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` in this diff). This is a verifiable copy/paste mismatch: it unnecessarily loads an unrelated job and fails to explicitly load the class under test. If `jobs/regular/process_post` is not present/loaded in the test environment, this require would raise a LoadError and break the spec.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb:13-23 — When topic_id is found but the topic has been deleted, TopicView.new may raise an exception with no handling for deleted/missing topics

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, the code treats the presence of a topic_id from TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) as sufficient to instantiate TopicView: `@topic_view = TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})`. However, topic_id_for_embed simply plucks an integer from the topic_embeds table and does not verify that the referenced Topic still exists. If the Topic record has been deleted/destroyed (or otherwise missing), this path will still run and will rely on TopicView to handle a nonexistent topic_id; in typical Rails/Discourse behavior this would raise (e.g., RecordNotFound / NotFound) and there is no rescue/fallback here (unlike the else path that enqueues retrieval). The lack of existence check/handling is directly observable in the diff and can cause a runtime exception for stale topic_embeds rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:30 — i.content is accessed without checking if it exists; SimpleRSS items may not always have a content field, causing NoMethodError for RSS feeds that only provide description
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the code assumes `i.content` is always present; in many RSS feeds it can be nil/missing, leading to a NoMethodError/nil dereference. The candidate also notes feeds may only provide `description`, aligning with the golden suggestion to fall back to `description` to avoid crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:41 — embed.post is accessed without checking if the associated post still exists; a deleted post would cause NoMethodError on the subsequent revisor call

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an existing TopicEmbed is found, the code does `post = embed.post` and then (if the SHA changed) unconditionally runs `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)`. If the associated Post record has been deleted (leaving an orphaned topic_embeds row; there is no FK shown and no dependent behavior in the diff), `embed.post` will be nil and PostRevisor will later call methods on @post (e.g., `@post.acting_user = ...`), causing an exception. There is no nil-check/cleanup for this case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:42 — PostRevisor#revise! is called with new_raw as the second argument but the updated signature expects new_raw to be a string of raw content; revisor revision may not respect cook_method: raw_html setting since post_revisor.rb doesn't set cook_method

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path calls `PostRevisor#revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), ...)`. `absolutize_urls` returns `fragment.to_html` (a String), which matches `PostRevisor#revise!(user, new_raw, opts={})`’s expected second argument. Also, `cook_method` is stored on the `Post` (set on creation via `PostCreator`), and `PostRevisor` does not reset it; `Post#cook` will still return `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`. Nothing in the diff shows a signature mismatch or loss of the `raw_html` cook behavior during revision.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb:45 — Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) is invoked synchronously from within perform_retrieve, which could block the RetrieveTopic worker on the entire feed poll and run outside the scheduler's intended context

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly (synchronously) when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs network I/O via `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and processes all `rss.items`, so invoking it inline will block the current execution (e.g., the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` worker triggered from EmbedController when no topic exists). This also bypasses the scheduled/recurrence intent of the scheduled job by running it ad-hoc during embed retrieval.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:13 — sidekiq_options retry: false with hourly recurrence means transient HTTP/network errors during open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) will silently drop that hour's poll with no alerting or logging

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the scheduled job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` and then does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no `rescue`. Any transient network/HTTP error from `open` (or parsing) will raise, causing the job run to fail and (because retries are disabled) it will not be retried, meaning that polling attempt is missed until the next hourly run. The "no alerting or logging" part isn’t strictly verifiable from the diff (Sidekiq will typically log exceptions), but the lack of retries/error handling is a real reliability issue introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:31 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) is vulnerable to SSRF; there's no validation that it's an http(s) URL or restriction against internal addresses
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same SSRF risk: PollFeed uses open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating/restricting the URL, allowing fetching arbitrary (including internal) resources if an attacker controls that setting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:55 — Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...) has no timeout, error handling, or response-size limit; a slow or huge remote page will hang the worker indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code does `open(url).read` and feeds the full body into `Readability::Document.new(...)` with no options (e.g., `open_timeout`, `read_timeout`) and no cap on how many bytes are read. This means a very large response will be fully slurped into memory and can tie up the job for a long time; network errors/timeouts will also raise and fail the job since there’s no rescue handling here. While Ruby/open-uri may have some defaults depending on version, the diff itself clearly introduces an unbounded remote fetch/read with no explicit limits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb:28 — ensure_embeddable only checks a single embeddable_host with no support for multiple allowed hosts/subdomains

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` intentionally enforces a single allowed host by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and the new site setting added is also singular (`embeddable_host: ''`). There is no stated requirement or prior behavior in the diff that multiple hosts/subdomains must be supported, so “no support for multiple allowed hosts/subdomains” is a feature request/design limitation, not a verifiable bug/defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js:11 — discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 for origin validation is substring-based and vulnerable to spoofing (e.g., http://eviltrout.com.evil.com would pass if discourseUrl is http://eviltrout.com); should use exact URL comparison
embed.html.erb:10 — parent.postMessage uses request.referer as targetOrigin; if referer is blank or invalid, postMessage silently fails to deliver with no fallback
best.html.erb:7 — @topic_view.topic.url is referenced even in the no posts branch; if topic_id_for_embed returns a topic with zero posts, .url may raise

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the `best.html.erb` template is only rendered in the branch where `topic_id` is present and `@topic_view = TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` is constructed. The alternate path (`topic_id` nil) renders `loading` instead. In `best.html.erb`, both header branches reference `@topic_view.topic.url`, but that does not depend on posts existing—if `TopicView` is successfully created, it is expected to have an associated `topic` regardless of whether `@topic_view.posts` is empty. The proposed finding assumes a scenario (topic returned but `@topic_view.topic` is nil / `.url` raises) that is not verifiable from this diff and would also likely fail earlier inside `TopicView.new` rather than only in the “no posts” branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller_spec.rb:50-52 — Test stubs TopicRetriever.new but the actual controller calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) asynchronously, not TopicRetriever directly; the test does not match the implementation

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` when no `topic_id` is found; it never calls `TopicRetriever.new` directly. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` expects `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` during the controller action. This is a direct mismatch with the implemented behavior and would cause the spec to fail (or test the wrong thing).

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_topic_embeds.rb:9 — embed_url is a string with no length limit; long URLs will truncate silently on MySQL or fail on insert depending on the adapter, with no explicit limit or model validation

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `create_topic_embeds`, `t.string :embed_url, null: false` does not specify a limit or any length validation in the model. In Rails, `:string` typically maps to a VARCHAR with an implicit default limit (commonly 255), so long embed URLs (which can easily exceed 255) may be rejected or truncated depending on DB/SQL mode. This is especially problematic because there is also a unique index on `embed_url`, so truncation could cause collisions. The finding’s core concern (missing explicit limit/validation leading to long-URL issues) is verifiable from the diff, even though the phrase “no length limit” is imprecise (there is an implicit default limit).

adjudication_records.issue_text: post_revisor.rb:14 — Removing the return false if not should_revise? line changes behavior for all callers, causing unnecessary post revisions/edits across the entire app — a regression unrelated to the stated intent

adjudication.rationale: The diff in lib/post_revisor.rb does not remove the guard `return false if not should_revise?`; it remains unchanged. The only change at that location is deletion of an extra blank line after the return, so behavior for callers is not altered and no regression is introduced by that hunk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:22 — The import appends I18n.t('embed.imported_from') with the raw URL inserted unescaped into an <a href='...'>; a malicious feed URL containing single quotes or HTML could break out of the attribute and inject markup

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, it appends `"#{url}"` into `contents` via `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: ...)` without any escaping. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which allows URLs containing single quotes or HTML (e.g. `http://a.com/'>`). Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for that method, and the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, injected markup would be rendered. This is a verifiable XSS/markup injection risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:60 — absolutize_urls only handles a and img relative URLs; other relative resources (srcset, CSS url(), source, video, iframe, etc.) are not absolutized, leading to broken resources

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls the code only rewrites relative paths for and . Feed-imported HTML (PollFeed uses i.content directly, and posts are rendered as raw_html) can include other URL-bearing attributes/tags (e.g., img[srcset], source[src], video[src], iframe[src], link[href], CSS url() in style attributes). Those would remain relative to Discourse rather than the original site, which can cause embedded resources to break. This limitation is directly verifiable from the method implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: site_settings.yml:354 — embeddable_host has no validation that it's actually a hostname (not a full URL); if an admin enters http://eviltrout.com, the host comparison will always fail and embedding will be silently broken

adjudication.rationale: The new embedding logic compares `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` directly against `URI(...).host` in two places: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` (`URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` (`SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`). `URI(...).host` returns only the hostname (e.g., `eviltrout.com`), so if an admin configures `embeddable_host` as a full URL like `http://eviltrout.com`, these comparisons will never match and embedding/retrieval will fail. The diff adds the setting but no validation/normalization to prevent this misconfiguration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:26 — User.where(username_lower: ...) returns nil silently if the configured embed_by_username user doesn't exist; the entire poll is silently skipped with no logging, making misconfiguration undetectable

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, poll_feed looks up the user via `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and immediately `return if user.blank?`. There is no logging, exception, or other signal when the configured `embed_by_username` does not correspond to an existing user, so the polling job will silently do nothing in that misconfigured state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated whitespace change in db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb causes scope drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff in db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb only removes trailing whitespace on a blank line and changes the file to have no trailing newline. There is no code logic change, no altered block structure, and nothing that would affect Ruby scope or behavior. This is at most a formatting/style change, not a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated force: true added to top_topics migration in db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. While `force: true` would drop an existing table if the migration were re-run, Rails migrations are applied once in order; on any database where this migration has already run, it will not be executed again, and on new databases the table won’t exist yet. So this is not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff; it’s at most an unnecessary/unrelated change or a hypothetical risk outside normal migration semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor removes the --category option and its handling, causing an unrelated functional regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes `method_option :category` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes all handling for `options[:category]` / `category_id`. Previously the importer could target a category by passing `category: category_id` into `PostCreator.new(...)`; now it always calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)` with no category parameter, so that CLI functionality is lost. This is a concrete, verifiable behavioral regression in the Disqus import task introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb mixes an unrelated cosmetic blank-line removal with the functional skip_validations change

adjudication.rationale: In lib/post_revisor.rb the diff removes a single blank line after `return false if not should_revise?` and also changes `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`. The blank-line removal is purely cosmetic and does not introduce any bug, security issue, or correctness defect; it only affects commit cleanliness/readability. The functional change is independent and valid on its own, so the finding is a style/process nit rather than a real problem in the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PR title mismatch: diff introduces a broad new embedding subsystem rather than just enhancing an existing validation system

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims a PR title mismatch (“embedding subsystem” vs “enhancing an existing validation system”), but the PR title is not provided anywhere in the diff. From the diff alone we can verify that an embedding/feed-import feature is being added (new EmbedController, TopicEmbed, jobs, assets, settings), but we cannot verify whether this conflicts with the PR title or intended scope. This is not a code bug/security/correctness defect that is demonstrably present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing trailing newlines in several new/modified files (embed.css.scss, embed.html.erb, loading.html.erb, migrate_word_counts.rb)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly marks “\ No newline at end of file” for embed.css.scss, app/views/embed/loading.html.erb, app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb, and db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb, so the observation is factually present. However, missing trailing newlines are generally a formatting/style nit rather than a bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded/unpaginated topic view retrieval: missing guard that the topic belongs to an embed context or is accessible to the embedding surface, leaking private/restricted topics

adjudication.rationale: The `embed#best` action does not accept a `topic_id` and can only build a `TopicView` for a topic reached via `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)`, i.e., one that has an explicit `topic_embeds` mapping for that `embed_url`. Also, it passes `{best: 5}`, so the retrieval is not unbounded/unpaginated. Whether `TopicView` enforces permissions/visibility for private topics is not shown in the diff, so the claimed “leaking private/restricted topics” via missing guards is not verifiable from this change set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer origin check in embed_controller.rb is substring-based and breaks when `request.referer` is missing, causing all legitimate embeds to fail

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the referer validation is **not substring-based**; it does an exact host comparison: `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. When `request.referer` is missing, `URI('')` yields a `nil` host, so the code raises `InvalidAccess` intentionally. This behavior is explicitly covered by the added spec (`"raises an error with no referer"`), indicating it’s a deliberate access control requirement, not an unintended defect causing “legitimate embeds” to fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` set globally without origin hardening; combined with substring-based `postMessage` origin check in embed.js, allows origin-validation bypass
TOCTOU race in `TopicEmbed.import`: `where` then `create` is not atomic, allowing duplicate topics and orphaned rows from concurrent jobs

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import` does a `where(embed_url: url).first` check before creating, but the subsequent creation is wrapped in `Topic.transaction` and the migration adds a **unique index** on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. Under concurrent execution, the second creator would hit `TopicEmbed.create!` raising (e.g., `RecordNotUnique`), and the surrounding transaction would roll back the topic/post it just created, preventing “duplicate topics” and “orphaned rows” as claimed. While a race can cause a transient exception/retry, the specific outcome described is not verifiably introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing foreign keys and no index on `topic_id` in `create_topic_embeds.rb` migration, leaving dangling records and linear lookups

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`, the new `topic_embeds` table defines `topic_id` and `post_id` columns but only adds an index on `embed_url` (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). There are no foreign key constraints to `topics`/`posts`, so the database would allow dangling `topic_embeds` rows if a topic/post is deleted. Also, there is no index on `topic_id` (or `post_id`), so lookups/joins filtering by `topic_id` would require a table scan, which matches the finding’s “linear lookups” claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `cook_method` has no DB-level CHECK constraint and uses a magic int default, allowing invalid values to be written directly

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `posts.cook_method` as an integer with default `1` and defines an enum-like mapping in `Post.cook_methods` (`:regular`, `:raw_html`). It’s true there is no DB CHECK constraint (and no explicit model inclusion validation in the diff), so in theory someone could write arbitrary integers via direct SQL. However, this is not a verifiable defect introduced here: Rails apps commonly rely on application-level enums without DB CHECKs, and the code path in `Post#cook` safely treats any non-`:raw_html` (including invalid integers) as the normal cooked pipeline. The “magic int default” is also consistent with how Discourse’s `Enum.new(...)` is typically used (existing `Post.types` works the same way), so there’s no demonstrated mismatch/bug in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `content_sha1` duplicates post content hash and is bypassed by other revision paths, causing it to drift and become stale

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `content_sha1` is introduced on `topic_embeds` and is only used inside `TopicEmbed.import` to detect whether the *source/imported* contents changed since the last import (`content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`) and then updated via `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` after a successful revise. There is no post-level content hash in this diff that it “duplicates”. While `content_sha1` can differ from the current `post.raw` if the post is edited through other paths (normal user edits), that drift is not a clearly verifiable defect here because the hash is tracking last-imported content, not necessarily current post content, and the import/update logic remains consistent with that purpose.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded materialization / no dedup pagination over the feed in `poll_feed.rb`: iterates entire feed with no cap, last-seen record, or etag usage

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then `rss.items.each do |i| ... TopicEmbed.import(...) end` with no limit, pagination, or “last seen” cutoff. The defined `feed_key` (likely intended for last-modified tracking) is never used, and there’s no ETag/Last-Modified conditional fetch logic. While `TopicEmbed.import` dedupes by `embed_url` (unique index) and avoids rewriting unchanged content via `content_sha1`, the job will still fetch and iterate the entire feed every run, which is an unbounded/performance issue directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 queries / no filtering of already-imported items in `poll_feed.rb`: each item calls `TopicEmbed.import` doing its own lookup

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job iterates `rss.items.each` and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for every item. `TopicEmbed.import` immediately performs `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`, i.e., at least one DB query per feed item. This is a verifiable per-item lookup pattern (O(N) queries) with no preloading/batching in `poll_feed` itself. However, the “no filtering of already-imported items” part is only partially accurate: `TopicEmbed.import` does check for an existing record and avoids creating duplicates (and only revises if the SHA1 changed), but it still incurs the lookup for each item every run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `i.content` can be nil/missing in `poll_feed.rb`, causing `NoMethodError` and aborting the entire feed import without per-item rescue

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is `nil` for an RSS/Atom item (which is possible depending on the feed fields available), calling `.scrub` on `nil` will raise `NoMethodError`, and there is no per-item rescue around the `rss.items.each` loop, so the entire job would abort on the first such item.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `poll_feed.rb` is SSRF-vulnerable and unauthenticated, lacking scheme/host allowlists, redirect caps, or timeouts

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (via `open-uri`) with no validation of scheme/host, no redirect limiting, and no explicit timeouts. `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` is not constrained to http/https in this diff, so it could be set to internal/localhost/metadata endpoints or even non-HTTP URIs supported by `open-uri`. Additionally, `TopicRetriever` can invoke `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` during embed retrieval, so remote requests to `/embed/best` can indirectly trigger this fetch when feed polling is enabled. This makes the lack of safeguards a real, verifiable issue introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously triggers full feed poll from within an on-demand job, coupling async paths and causing inefficiency

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it directly calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (synchronously, in-process) before proceeding to HTTP fetch. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does a full `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` + `SimpleRSS.parse` and iterates `rss.items.each` importing each item. This means each on-demand retrieve (triggered via `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` from `EmbedController#best`) can run a full feed poll, coupling the scheduled-feed-import path into the on-demand retrieval path and potentially doing expensive work repeatedly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Throttle in `topic_retriever.rb` uses Redis `setnx`/`expire` non-atomically, risking a permanent lock if a crash occurs between the two calls

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then given a TTL via a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two calls are not atomic; if the process crashes (or the thread dies) after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will remain without an expiration. Subsequent calls will see `setnx` fail and return `true` (throttled) indefinitely for that `@embed_url`, effectively creating a permanent lock until the key is manually deleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `import_remote` uses `open(url).read` with no scheme/host validation, creating an SSRF/XXE vector via the Disqus path

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code does `open(url).read` without any validation of the URL scheme/host (no `http/https` check, no allowlist). This method is invoked from the Disqus import task (`lib/tasks/disqus.thor`) as `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, where `t[:link]` comes from the imported Disqus data. That means a crafted Disqus export could cause the importer to fetch arbitrary URLs (including internal network endpoints), which is a verifiable SSRF risk introduced by this diff. (The diff does not clearly demonstrate an XXE specifically, but the unvalidated outbound fetch is real.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: `raw_html` cook method bypasses the sanitization pipeline entirely, causing stored XSS in the embed surface when rendering unescaped RSS/HTML content

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `Post.cook_methods` enum and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which is typically where sanitization occurs). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and populates `raw` from feed/remote HTML (`contents` from RSS via `Jobs::PollFeed` uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` with no sanitization). The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked`, and for these posts `cooked == raw`, so attacker-controlled HTML from an RSS/ATOM feed can be stored and rendered as-is, enabling stored XSS in the embed output (and potentially anywhere else that renders `post.cooked` as HTML).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `postMessage` targetOrigin in `embed.html.erb` is `request.referer`, leaking embed height/structure to any parent and risking errors if referer is nil/invalid

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb the code calls parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>'). The second argument to postMessage must be a valid targetOrigin (e.g., "https://example.com" or "*") and browsers treat strings containing a path/query (a full referer URL like "http://eviltrout.com/2013/..."), or an empty string from nil, as an invalid origin and will throw a DOMException / fail to send the message. So this is a real correctness bug introduced by using request.referer directly instead of its origin; the "leaking" framing is less accurate, but the invalid/nil targetOrigin problem is verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` in `best.html.erb` assume `user` is non-nil and loaded per post, causing N+1 queries and crashes for deleted users

adjudication.rationale: In the new `best.html.erb` the template calls `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username`, but the diff does not show how `@topic_view.posts` are loaded. `TopicView` in Discourse typically loads posts with their associated users preloaded, so an N+1 is not verifiable from this diff. Also, Discourse posts generally have a non-null `user_id` and deleted users are usually represented by an existing (anonymized/system) user record rather than `post.user` being `nil`, so a crash for “deleted users” is not a demonstrated defect in the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `skip_validations: true` on imported posts bypasses rate limits, spam checks, and required metadata, creating a validation-free write surface

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a deliberate validation bypass for embedded/imported content. In `TopicEmbed.import`, new posts are created via `PostCreator.new(..., skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`, and updates use `PostRevisor#revise!` with `skip_validations: true` (and also `bypass_rate_limiter: true`). The diff also changes `PostRevisor#update_post` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, making `skip_validations` actually disable ActiveRecord validations on revision saves. While the claim about “spam checks” isn’t directly shown in this diff, the existence of a validation-free write path (and explicit rate limiter bypass on revise) is verifiably present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` in `post_revisor.rb` changes default revision semantics, allowing any future caller to unintentionally bypass validations

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` (always validates) to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`. However, the default behavior when `opts` does not include `:skip_validations` is unchanged because `!nil` is `true`, so validations still run. Validations are only bypassed when a caller *explicitly* passes `skip_validations: true` (as the new `TopicEmbed.import` code does), which appears intentional for imports. The finding’s claim that it changes “default revision semantics” and could be bypassed “unintentionally” is not directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: User lookup by `username_lower` in `topic_retriever.rb` is not fail-fast validated; if the setting names a non-existent user, the embed never completes

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, the code looks up `user = User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and then silently `return if user.blank?` without raising/logging. The only gating checks elsewhere (`PollFeed#execute`) require `embed_by_username.present?` but do not verify the user exists. As a result, when `embed_by_username` is set to a non-existent user, `EmbedController#best` will enqueue retrieval and render `loading`, but the retriever will always bail out and no `TopicEmbed` will ever be created—so the embed will keep reloading indefinitely with no fail-fast error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `absolutize_urls` in `topic_embed.rb` only handles `href`/`src` starting with `/`, missing protocol-relative URLs, `../` paths, and srcset attributes

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the new `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` method, URLs are only rewritten when `href`/`src` start with `/`. That means other relative forms like `../foo`, `images/foo`, or `?x=1` are not converted at all despite the comment claiming to convert “any relative URLs,” so embedded/imported HTML can contain broken links/images. Additionally, protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png` also start with `/` and will be incorrectly rewritten to `#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/x.png` (changing the host), which is a concrete correctness bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` in `embed.js` is a substring-origin bug, allowing spoofed origins that contain the discourse URL substring
`force: true` added to existing migration `create_top_topics.rb` is destructive and not idempotent-safe across rolling deploys
Trailing newline removed in `migrate_word_counts.rb` and whitespace-only diff mixes unrelated concerns into the PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` now ends with `\ No newline at end of file`, so the trailing newline was removed, and it also includes whitespace-only changes (e.g., removing trailing spaces). However, this is a formatting/style nit and does not introduce a functional bug, security issue, or correctness defect in the code. The claim about “mixes unrelated concerns into the PR” is also a process/style critique rather than a verifiable code defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `import_remote` in the Disqus path has no `embeddable_host` check, allowing off-host links to be fetched and imported, muddling the ownership boundary

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` indeed does not reference `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but in the code paths added here the host restriction is enforced one layer up: `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` blocks retrieval unless `URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` before calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. The remaining caller is `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, which is an admin-run import task and is not part of the embedding boundary enforced by `embeddable_host` in this diff. So the finding’s implication that this enables off-host fetching/importing via the embedding feature is not verifiably true from the diff (it would only happen if an operator runs the Disqus task on arbitrary links, which is a different trust boundary).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `belongs_to :topic` / `:post` in `topic_embed.rb` lacks `optional`/inverse and no uniqueness on `post_id`, allowing multiple embed rows per topic

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `topic_embeds` enforces uniqueness on `embed_url` via a unique index, and all lookup/update logic is keyed by `embed_url` (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and `topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)`). There is no demonstrated correctness or security issue caused by not having uniqueness on `post_id`/`topic_id`; allowing multiple `TopicEmbed` rows per topic/post is not shown to break any behavior introduced here. Also, `belongs_to` lacking `optional:`/`inverse_of` is not a verifiable defect in this Rails 4-era code (those are not required for correctness and `optional:` is primarily a Rails 5+ validation behavior change).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb: Unrelated `force: true` in `create_table` is destructive and causes data loss if the table exists.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails/ActiveRecord, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, which is destructive and can cause data loss if `top_topics` exists at migration time (where previously it would have raised an error instead of dropping data).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb: Contains unrelated whitespace changes and removes the newline at the end of the file.

adjudication.rationale: The diff for db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb does show (1) an unrelated whitespace-only change (a trailing-space removal on a blank line) and (2) the file now lacks a trailing newline ("\\ No newline at end of file"). However, these are formatting/style issues and do not introduce a bug, security issue, or correctness defect in the migration logic itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor: Refactoring Disqus import to use `TopicEmbed.import_remote` causes functional regression by dropping support for the `category` option and ignoring original `created_at` timestamps.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the `method_option :category` line and all logic that resolved `category_id` from `options[:category]` were removed. The creation call changed from `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not pass `category` or `created_at`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import` ultimately use `PostCreator.new(... raw: ..., skip_validations: true, cook_method: ...)` without setting `created_at` or category. So the diff verifiably drops category support and no longer preserves original timestamps during Disqus import.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js: `postMessage` origin validation uses `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, which is a flawed security pattern allowing substring matches to bypass instead of exact origin matching.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue flag the same security flaw: using indexOf/substring-based origin validation for postMessage is insufficient and can be bypassed by malicious origins that contain the expected domain as a substring (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb: `i.content.scrub` is called without checking if `i.content` is present, causing a `NoMethodError` if an RSS/Atom feed item lacks a content field.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, inside `rss.items.each`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item does not have a `content` field, `i.content` can be `nil`, and calling `.scrub` on `nil` will raise `NoMethodError`. There is no presence check or fallback (e.g., `i.description`) before calling `.scrub`, so this is a real runtime correctness bug introduced by the diff for feeds lacking `content`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb: `absolutize_urls` hardcodes ports 80 and 443, failing for non-standard configurations and incorrectly appending ports; should use `uri.default_port`.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the prefix appends ":#{uri.port}" only when uri.port is not 80 and not 443. Since urls are allowed for both http and https, this logic fails for non-standard combinations like `https://example.com:80/...` (uri.port == 80 so it will NOT append, producing wrong absolute URLs) or `http://example.com:443/...` (uri.port == 443 so it will NOT append). The correct check is whether `uri.port != uri.default_port`, not membership in {80,443}. This is a concrete correctness bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS vulnerability: RSS feed content is stored and rendered as raw HTML without any sanitization, allowing attackers to inject script tags via the RSS feed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `:raw_html` cook method that makes `Post#cook` return `raw` directly (skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline). `Jobs::PollFeed` takes `i.content` from the RSS feed, only does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and passes it into `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In the embed view, the post content is rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. There is no sanitization step for RSS-provided HTML, so malicious markup (e.g., `<script>`) in feed content would be stored and rendered as-is, enabling stored XSS in the embedded/Discourse context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS vulnerability: URL is interpolated unescaped into an `<a href>` attribute in the imported_from footer, allowing attribute injection via malicious URLs.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")` directly into `contents`. Although it checks `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, that only enforces the scheme/prefix and does not prevent quotes or other characters that can break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute (e.g., `http://example.com/' onclick='alert(1)`). Because these imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` (no sanitization), and the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, making this a stored XSS/attribute injection vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS vulnerability: `javascript:` URI schemes are not stripped from Readability-extracted links, allowing execution of attacker-controlled JavaScript when clicked.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses ruby-readability to extract HTML allowing `<a>` tags with `href` attributes, then `TopicEmbed.import` stores that HTML as a post with `cook_method: :raw_html`. In `Post#cook`, `:raw_html` returns `raw` directly, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The only processing done is `absolutize_urls`, which rewrites only relative URLs starting with `/` and does not strip or validate schemes like `javascript:`. Therefore, a source page containing `<a href="javascript:...">` can result in stored content that executes attacker-controlled JS when clicked.
